newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian judge orders ex-SS major free.
newsitem.headline: Italian judge orders ex-SS major free.

text.p: A military judge on Thursday ordered the release from house arrest of a former SS major suspected of involvement in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity and ruled that his case should instead be considered by the civil judiciary.

The ruling on 84-year-old Karl Hass after a closed-door committal hearing could create a legal nightmare. Another former SS officer, ex-captain Erich Priebke, is in preventive detention pending a re-trial by a military court over the same atrocity.

Military prosecutor Antonino Intelisano had asked Thursday's hearing to charge Hass with complicity in mulitiple murder and put him on trial alongside Priebke over the SS massacre of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves outside Rome in March 1944.
The committal judge, Giuseppe Mazzi, instead accepted a petition from lawyers representing relatives of the victims that the case should be considered by civil courts.

Hass has been living under police supervision at a clinic where he is recovering from a fractured pelvis suffered last June when he tried to clamber over a hotel balcony and flee on the eve of testimony as a witness at Priebke's original trial.

Priebke's trial ended in a controversial verdict that he was guilty of multiple murder but could not be punished. Italy's highest court, the Court of Cassation, quashed the verdict and ordered a new military trial for Priebke in October.
